one_liner: Enterprise CRM and application platform for managing sales, service, marketing and custom business processes.
self_serve_evidence: A free, self-serve Developer Edition org gives instant OAuth-based API access, but on paid production orgs API access is bundled only into Enterprise/Unlimited/Performance editions, while Professional Edition requires contacting an Account Executive to purchase the Web Services API add-on, and Group/Essentials editions cannot get API access at all.
api_surface: REST, SOAP, Bulk, Streaming and Metadata APIs, extremely broad — hundreds of standard and custom sObject types, fully metadata-driven.
existing_mcp_detail: Official salesforcecli/mcp (GitHub) plus Salesforce's hosted Agentforce MCP servers described at developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/mcp.html.
notes: Free Developer Edition org (developer.salesforce.com/signup) is the fastest self-serve path to real API credentials; production customers on lower editions face edition-based gating; Salesforce is restricting creation of new 'Connected Apps' as of Spring '26 in favor of External Client Apps.

one_liner: All-in-one marketing, sales, service and CMS platform built around a CRM core.
self_serve_evidence: A free HubSpot account holder (as super admin) can create a private app from Settings > Integrations and get a bearer access token instantly, no sales contact needed.
api_surface: REST, very broad — CRM objects (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, custom objects), plus Marketing, CMS, Conversations and Automation APIs.
existing_mcp_detail: Official HubSpot Remote MCP Server, public beta, documented at developers.hubspot.com/ai-tools/mcp.
notes: Free/Starter tier private apps are rate-limited to 100 requests per 10 seconds; higher limits on paid tiers.

one_liner: Sales-pipeline-centric CRM built for small and mid-size sales teams.
self_serve_evidence: A free trial account gets an API token immediately from Settings > Personal Preferences > API, no approval process.
api_surface: REST (v1 and v2), broad — deals, persons, organizations, activities, products, leads, pipelines and more.
existing_mcp_detail: Native official Pipedrive MCP Server (pipedrive.com/en/features/mcp-server) built and maintained by Pipedrive, available on all plans via OAuth; also multiple community MCP servers exist.
notes: Only one active API token per user at a time when using token auth; OAuth2 is the recommended path for published marketplace apps.

one_liner: Modern, highly customizable relationship-intelligence CRM aimed at fast-moving teams.
self_serve_evidence: Attio's Free plan includes API and webhook access, and a workspace API key can be generated instantly from developer settings with no sales contact.
api_surface: REST API v2, moderately broad — objects, records, lists, notes, tasks, workspace members, webhooks.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Attio MCP documented at docs.attio.com/mcp/overview; also several community servers.
notes: Supports both single-workspace API keys and multi-workspace OAuth2 apps for published integrations.

one_liner: Open-source, self-hostable CRM positioned as a modern alternative to Salesforce.
self_serve_evidence: Any workspace member can create an API key instantly under Settings > API & Webhooks (Bearer token auth), and since Twenty is fully open source it can also be self-hosted with zero gatekeeping.
api_surface: REST and GraphQL, schema-per-tenant — endpoints are auto-generated for built-in objects (People, Companies, Opportunities) and any custom objects, plus a Metadata API to manage schema.
existing_mcp_detail: Community MCP servers exist (e.g. realboost/twenty-mcp-server); no official vendor-shipped MCP server found as of research date.
notes: Rate limit ~100 requests/minute, batch operations up to 60 records; open-source self-hosting removes all commercial gating entirely. [Verified] Twenty is open-core: AGPLv3 core + separate commercial license for Enterprise-marked features (not unconditionally 'fully open source').

one_liner: Highly customizable work-management/workspace platform (with CRM-style apps) owned by Progress Software.
self_serve_evidence: Any signed-in Podio user can generate an API key directly from account settings, with no manual approval step described in current docs.
api_surface: REST, very broad — items, apps, tasks, files, comments, hooks/webhooks, organizations; generic since Podio itself is a customizable no-code workspace tool.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Podio MCP Server hosted at mcp.podio.com, operated by Progress Software, supporting Claude, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot Studio.
notes: Quick-start default credentials are capped at roughly 30-40 requests (meant for testing); production use requires registering a Client ID/Secret for higher limits.

one_liner: Zoho's full-featured cloud CRM for sales, marketing and customer engagement, part of the broader Zoho suite.
self_serve_evidence: The Free CRM plan itself lists 'APIs — connect Zoho CRM to any app' with 5,000 calls/day, and Zoho's 'Self Client' OAuth flow lets a developer generate access/refresh tokens directly from the API console without any review process.
api_surface: REST API v8, very broad — leads, deals, contacts, custom modules, COQL query language, bulk read/write APIs, notifications.
existing_mcp_detail: Zoho MCP (zoho.com/mcp) is an official offering spanning CRM plus other Zoho apps (Mail, Desk, Projects, etc.); community alternative also exists.
notes: Access tokens expire after 1 hour requiring refresh-token flow; multiple regional data-center domains (.com, .eu, .in, .com.cn, etc.) change the API base URL per account.

one_liner: Inside-sales CRM built around built-in calling, emailing and SMS workflows for SMB sales teams.
self_serve_evidence: A free 14-day trial account can generate an API key immediately under Settings > Developer > API Keys, sent via HTTP Basic auth, with no approval step.
api_surface: REST, broad — leads, contacts, opportunities, tasks, calls, SMS, email sequences, custom activities and reporting.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Close MCP Server documented at help.close.com/docs/mcp-server.
notes: API keys are recommended for internal/scripted use; OAuth2 is recommended for apps that need user consent or will be published externally.

one_liner: CRM built natively into Google Workspace for relationship-driven sales teams.
self_serve_evidence: Any individual user can self-serve generate a personal API token instantly from System Settings > API Keys, but the docs describe OAuth2 as 'the preferred approach for partner integrations,' implying a more formal path for apps meant to be published/distributed to other Copper customers.
api_surface: REST API v1, moderately broad — leads, people, companies, opportunities, projects, tasks, activities.
existing_mcp_detail: Only third-party/community MCP integrations found; no official Copper-branded MCP server located.
blocker: none for a single-workspace agent using a personal API key; formal partner approval likely needed only to publish a multi-tenant OAuth app.
notes: Could not directly fetch Copper's own pricing/trial page to confirm free-trial API availability; conclusion is based on the developer docs plus third-party pricing summaries found via search.

one_liner: CRM and deal-management platform (by Intapp) purpose-built for private equity, investment banking and other capital-markets firms.
self_serve_evidence: DealCloud is sold exclusively through enterprise sales cycles (third-party pricing data shows contracts from ~$85K to ~$1.4M/year, avg ~$505K ACV) with no public signup or free trial; API client_id/apiKey credentials are only issued to provisioned client site instances.
api_surface: REST, broad — Data & Schema API, User Management API, Publications API, Relationship Intelligence Import API, Site Backup API; official SDKs (e.g. Python) also available.
existing_mcp_detail: Official DealCloud MCP Server announced at api.docs.dealcloud.com/mcp, described as in 'client preview' starting July 2026 (not yet broadly GA).
blocker: Requires being an existing paying enterprise DealCloud customer (six-to-seven-figure annual contract) to obtain any API credentials; no self-serve trial, sandbox, or public developer signup exists.
notes: Pricing/gating evidence comes from a third-party source (Vendr) rather than DealCloud's own site, since DealCloud does not publish pricing; auth/API documentation itself was fetched directly and is well documented technically.

one_liner: Cloud-based customer service platform for ticketing, live chat, help center, and omnichannel support.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are self-generated in Admin Center (Apps and integrations > APIs), and Zendesk explicitly offers trial/sponsored developer accounts for building integrations.
api_surface: Broad REST API (developer.zendesk.com/api-reference) covering Ticketing, Help Center, Chat, Talk, and more, with hundreds of documented endpoints; Basic Auth/API-token method is deprecated in favor of OAuth Bearer tokens.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist; Zendesk's own 'MCP client' feature lets Zendesk AI agents consume external MCP servers rather than exposing an official first-party MCP server for the Zendesk API itself.
notes: Legacy API-token+Basic-Auth method is deprecated (Zendesk pushing OAuth); sandbox environments and trial/sponsored dev accounts are available.

one_liner: AI-first customer messaging, chat, and helpdesk platform built around the Fin AI agent.
self_serve_evidence: An access token is issued automatically as soon as a developer creates an app in the Intercom Developer Hub, no approval needed for private-app/own-workspace access.
api_surface: Broad REST API (conversations, contacts, tickets, articles, etc.) plus a dedicated Fin Agent API and Canvas Kit for building in-app experiences.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Intercom/Fin MCP Server documented at developers.intercom.com/docs/guides/mcp.
notes: OAuth required only when building a public app that accesses other workspaces' data; free trial available for new workspaces to obtain a dev app.

one_liner: Cloud helpdesk and ticketing software for customer support teams.
self_serve_evidence: API key is visible directly in the agent's Profile Settings in the support portal, with no approval step, and a free trial account can be created to obtain one.
api_surface: REST API (developer.freshdesk.com) covering tickets, contacts, agents, companies, forums, solutions, surveys, and groups.
existing_mcp_detail: Freshdesk shipped a native MCP integration as an Early Access Program feature; community server effytech/freshdesk_mcp also exists.
notes: Official MCP is still in Early Access Program (EAP), so may require enabling/opt-in; API key auth format is 'apikey:X'.

one_liner: Shared inbox / customer communication hub unifying email and omnichannel messages for support teams.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are self-serve from account settings for single-workspace/internal use, but OAuth2 (required for public, multi-customer App Store integrations) needs Front's app framework and 'an exception' approval for non-OAuth public apps.
api_surface: Broad REST 'Core API' covering conversations, contacts, inboxes, rules, tags, and teams, with token scopes split across features/namespaces/permissions; also exposes an MCP server.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Front MCP server (beta) documented at dev.frontapp.com/docs/mcp-server.
blocker: Distributing a public/multi-tenant integration requires OAuth2 plus Front App Store review (or an explicit exception); single-workspace token access is unrestricted.
notes: MCP server access itself is one of the token 'features' that can be scoped/limited, suggesting fine-grained control for agent use cases.

one_liner: Modern B2B customer support platform (tickets, Slack/Teams-based support, shared Slack channels) built for SaaS companies.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are generated directly from the Pylon dashboard settings page with no mention of approval or a required paid tier, and can be verified immediately via the /me endpoint.
api_surface: REST API (docs.usepylon.com) covering accounts, teams, issues, and more; documented breadth is moderate compared to older incumbents.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Pylon MCP server documented at docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/pylon-mcp.
notes: Authentication page itself is sparse on endpoint breadth details; full API reference exists separately.

one_liner: Help desk software combining ticketing, live chat, and call center features.
self_serve_evidence: API keys are self-generated in Configuration > System > API for existing accounts, but the number of allowed keys is gated by paid plan tier (1 key on Small Business up to 100 on Enterprise) and it's unclear if API access is enabled during the 30-day free trial.
api_surface: REST API (v3 current, v1 legacy) covering ticketing, chat, and call-center functionality; documented with filtering support.
existing_mcp_detail: Official LiveAgent MCP server from parent company QualityUnit (github.com/QualityUnit/liveagent-mcp-server).
blocker: API key quota/availability is tied to paid plan tier, and free-trial API access is unconfirmed.
notes: 30-day free trial advertised (no credit card), but pricing page shows API keys as a paid-plan line item rather than a trial feature.

one_liner: API-first, GraphQL-native customer support tool built for software/B2B companies.
self_serve_evidence: A developer can create a Machine User and API key directly from Settings in the Plain dashboard with selectable permissions, with no sales/approval step documented.
api_surface: Single GraphQL API (core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1) that Plain says has 'no limitations in what can be done via the API vs the UI', i.e. very broad coverage of the product.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Plain MCP server announced at plain.com/blog/mcp-server and plain.com/changelog/plain-mcp.
notes: GraphQL-only API (no separate REST surface); pricing/free-tier details weren't confirmed on the docs pages fetched, only self-serve key creation.

one_liner: Help desk and shared-inbox software for customer support teams.
self_serve_evidence: Developers create an OAuth2 app themselves via Profile > My Apps > 'Create My App' with no approval process mentioned, and a free trial account is available to sign up.
api_surface: Broad REST Mailbox API (conversations, customers, inboxes, attachments, custom fields, tags, reports, webhooks, workflows, teams) plus a separate Docs API.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Help Scout MCP server (beta) at mcp-beta.helpscout.net.
notes: OAuth2-only (no plain API key/basic auth); both Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows supported; credentials must be tied to an active invited user.

one_liner: Ecommerce-focused helpdesk/customer support platform with deep Shopify/BigCommerce integration.
self_serve_evidence: Private-app API key auth (email + API key) is self-serve and testable directly in the API docs, while OAuth2 is reserved for public/delegated apps which typically require Gorgias partner/app-review approval.
api_surface: REST API (developers.gorgias.com) covering tickets, customers, integrations, and ecommerce-context resources; interactive docs allow live testing.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Gorgias MCP server in Open Beta.
notes: Public/multi-tenant OAuth2 apps likely require Gorgias app-store review, adding friction beyond basic private-app API key use.

one_liner: AI-native, enterprise customer service platform organized around a single lifelong customer conversation/timeline.
self_serve_evidence: API access requires being an existing paying Gladly customer with an admin who grants a user the 'API User' permission to generate tokens; there is no public self-serve signup, published pricing, or free trial found.
api_surface: Broad REST API (developer.gladly.com/rest) covering customer profiles, conversations/timeline, comms (SMS/email), knowledge/answers, agents, inboxes, business hours, analytics/exports, tasks, and webhooks, plus a separate sandbox domain and an App Platform (appcfg CLI) for config-based apps.
existing_mcp_detail: No official Gladly MCP server found; only third-party integration/connector listings surfaced.
blocker: No public self-serve trial or pricing — a developer must already be a contracted Gladly customer (enterprise sales) and get admin-granted API User permission before any credentials can be issued.
notes: Docs reference a QA/sandbox environment, but both still presuppose an existing organization domain, i.e. an existing paid account.

one_liner: Team messaging and collaboration platform with channels, DMs, and an extensive app/bot ecosystem.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can create apps and generate OAuth tokens instantly at api.slack.com/apps; public distribution/marketplace listing requires a separate app review, but building and using an app in your own workspace is immediate.
api_surface: Broad REST Web API (chat, channels, users, files, canvases) plus Events API, Socket Mode, and RTM; hundreds of methods across dozens of scopes.
existing_mcp_detail: Slack has an official MCP server enabling assistants like Claude/Perplexity to search and act in Slack; community servers like korotovsky/slack-mcp-server also exist.
notes: OAuth scopes tightly govern access; public app distribution/marketplace listing requires Slack app review, but self-workspace integrations are frictionless.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform providing programmable SMS, voice, video, and verification APIs.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can sign up for a free trial account instantly and get Account SID/Auth Token or create API keys via the Console without approval.
api_surface: Very broad REST API spanning Voice, Messaging (SMS/MMS/WhatsApp), Verify, phone number provisioning, SIP, and usage/account management.
existing_mcp_detail: Official twilio-labs/mcp monorepo (published as @twilio-alpha/mcp) exposes Twilio's API as MCP tools.
notes: Production use of phone numbers/messaging may require A2P 10DLC registration depending on country, but core API access itself is immediately self-serve with a trial account.

one_liner: Business team-chat and collaboration app from Zoho with bots, channels, and messaging APIs.
self_serve_evidence: Developers register apps in the Zoho API Console and complete the OAuth2 authorization-code flow themselves without manual approval for standard scopes.
api_surface: REST API v2/v3 covering channels, messages, chats, bots, and webhooks; moderate breadth, well documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Zoho publishes an official Cliq MCP server supporting Claude, Cursor, VS, Windsurf clients for messaging/reminders/channel management.
notes: Access tokens expire hourly requiring refresh-token handling.

one_liner: All-in-one enterprise collaboration suite (chat, docs, calendar, base) from ByteDance with an open platform API.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can register a custom app on open.larksuite.com and obtain App ID/App Secret (tenant token) or run OAuth2 for user tokens without needing manual approval for internal/custom apps.
api_surface: Extensive Server API (REST, tenant_access_token / user_access_token) covering messaging, docs, calendar, approval, contacts, and more across the whole Lark/Feishu suite.
existing_mcp_detail: Official larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp (published as @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp) wraps the Open Platform API as MCP tools.
notes: Publishing an app for external/public distribution goes through app review; internal/custom app development is immediate.

one_liner: Free team chat app (Slack alternative) from CAKE.com with channels, DMs, and workflow integrations.
self_serve_evidence: Any workspace member can generate an API key themselves via the built-in '/api-keys generate' slash command or the API Keys addon, no approval needed.
api_surface: Moderate REST API (via the 'API Keys' addon/Swagger docs) covering sending messages, replies, reactions, message deletion, channel creation/listing, and DMs; rate-limited to 1000 req/min per user.
existing_mcp_detail: Community MCP servers exist; no official Pumble/CAKE.com MCP found.
notes: API is delivered as an 'addon' (CAKE.com marketplace) rather than a first-class top-level API product.

one_liner: Voice, video, and text chat platform originally built for gaming communities, now widely used for community/team communication.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can create an application and bot in the Discord Developer Portal instantly, generate a bot token, and start calling the API with no approval step for standard bot scopes.
api_surface: Broad HTTP REST API plus a real-time Gateway (WebSocket) covering messages, channels, guilds, interactions (slash commands, components, modals), and monetization.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers; no official Discord-maintained MCP server was found.
notes: Bots requiring 'privileged intents' or verification at 100+ servers require Discord approval; small-scale/dev use is fully self-serve.

one_liner: Cloud-based messaging app with a public Bot API for building chatbots and automations.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can create a bot instantly by messaging @BotFather to receive an auth token, no application review or approval required.
api_surface: Comprehensive Bot API covering messages, media, inline queries, polls, payments, business features, and chat/admin management; separate lower-level MTProto client API also exists.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community MCP servers exist; no official Telegram-maintained MCP server found.
notes: Bot API is distinct from the raw MTProto/user Client API; Bot API itself is fully sanctioned self-serve.

one_liner: Meta's business messaging API (Cloud API) enabling companies to send/receive WhatsApp messages at scale.
self_serve_evidence: Initial testing (temporary tokens, test numbers) can be set up self-serve via the Meta App Dashboard, but production use requires a permanent System User token, a connected WhatsApp Business Account, and Meta Business/App verification plus phone number display-name approval before scaling beyond limited messaging tiers.
api_surface: REST-based Graph API for sending template/session messages, receiving webhooks, media, and (newer) group/calling features; broad but tightly governed by messaging policies and conversation-based pricing.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers wrap the official Cloud API; Meta has not published an official MCP server.
blocker: Meta Business verification and permanent-token/System-User setup gate production access; unverified businesses are capped on messaging volume and template approval.
notes: Sandbox/dev testing is quick and self-serve; the well-known friction is business verification, message template approval, and per-conversation pricing/rate tiers.

one_liner: Cloud-based business phone system and call center software with an API for calls, contacts, and messaging.
self_serve_evidence: Existing Aircall customers can self-serve generate api_id/api_token (Basic Auth) from Company Settings for their own account, but building a public multi-tenant integration requires OAuth2 credentials obtained only by applying to and being approved for Aircall's Tech Partner program.
api_surface: REST API (v1/v2) covering users, teams, calls, contacts, numbers, SMS/MMS/WhatsApp messaging, conversation intelligence (transcripts, sentiment), dialer campaigns, webhooks, and analytics; rate-limited to 120 req/min/company.
existing_mcp_detail: Unofficial community MCP server (73 tools) exists; no official Aircall-maintained MCP server found.
blocker: Public/OAuth-based integrations require approval into Aircall's Tech Partner program; single-account Basic Auth access is self-serve but not usable for a multi-tenant agent-toolkit product.
notes: For a toolkit meant to serve many customers, the Tech Partner approval requirement is the key friction; a single-workspace integration is otherwise straightforward via Basic Auth.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform (formerly Nexmo) offering programmable Voice, SMS, Verify, and Number Insight APIs.
self_serve_evidence: Developers sign up for an account and immediately receive an API key/secret from the Developer Dashboard or CLI, with free starting credit and no approval gate for core API access.
api_surface: Broad REST API portfolio covering Voice, SMS/Messages, Verify (2FA), Number Insight, and virtual number provisioning; JWT required for webhook-receiving APIs (e.g., Voice), Basic Auth/API key for simpler APIs like SMS.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Vonage-maintained MCP servers: Vonage-Community/telephony-mcp-server and Vonage/vonage-mcp-server-documentation.
notes: Some newer/regulated capabilities may need additional carrier or account-level enablement, but the core communications APIs are immediately self-serve.

one_liner: Google's advertising platform API for programmatically creating, managing, and reporting on Google Ads campaigns.
self_serve_evidence: Test/Explorer access levels are auto-granted self-serve, but Basic Access (~5 business days) and Standard Access (~10 business days, unlimited quota) require a developer-token application reviewed via the API Center, with brand verification possible.
api_surface: REST and gRPC API using Google Ads Query Language (GAQL); broad surface covering campaigns, ad groups, keywords, billing, reporting across dozens of resources/services.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Google-maintained server at github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp (search, resource metadata, list_accessible_customers tools, OAuth/ADC auth).
blocker: Developer token approval (Basic/Standard access) required for production use beyond limited Explorer/test tiers; process takes 5-10 business days and requires manager account setup.
notes: Explorer access (auto-granted) is enough for light production use at low volume (2,880 ops/day); serious agent tooling will need Basic Access at minimum.

one_liner: Meta's Marketing API for creating, managing, and analyzing Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns.
self_serve_evidence: Full Access (formerly Advanced Access, needed for real ads_management usage) requires App Review plus demonstrating 500+ Marketing API calls in 15 days with <15% error rate; default Limited Access has low rate limits.
api_surface: REST-style Graph API; broad surface covering campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives, audiences, insights/reporting, catalogs, and Conversions API.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers (135 tools in some); no official Meta-maintained MCP found.
blocker: App Review / Full Access tier gating requires prior usage history and passing Meta's review, which is a real approval gate for production ad management.
notes: System User tokens (non-expiring) make server-to-server automation feasible once access tier is approved.

one_liner: LinkedIn's Marketing API suite for managing ad campaigns, lead sync, audience targeting, and conversion tracking.
self_serve_evidence: Only baseline permissions (profile, email, w_member_social) are self-serve; the Advertising API product requires applying through the Developer Portal and becoming an approved partner, with Matched Audiences requiring approved partner status.
api_surface: REST APIs spanning campaign management, reporting/analytics, Lead Sync, Matched Audiences, Conversions API, and company/community management — moderately broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community servers exist; no official LinkedIn MCP found.
blocker: Marketing API access is not self-serve — it requires formal partner-program application and approval by LinkedIn, with no guaranteed timeline.
notes: This is one of the strictest gates among the 10 apps studied; approval is discretionary and relationship-based, not purely criteria-based like Google/Meta.

one_liner: All-in-one CRM/marketing automation platform (funnels, CRM, calendars, SMS/email) for agencies and SMBs.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can instantly sign up on the Marketplace developer portal, create an app, and receive OAuth2 Client ID/Secret immediately for Private app use; public Marketplace listing is optional and only reviewed at that later stage.
api_surface: REST API (v2) covering CRM/contacts, opportunities/pipelines, calendars/appointments, messaging (SMS/email/calls), payments, workflows, and 50+ webhook events — broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Numerous community MCP servers with OAuth support; no official HighLevel MCP found.
notes: Private integration tokens are also supported as a simpler non-OAuth auth alternative for single-account use.

one_liner: Email marketing and marketing automation platform for building campaigns and managing subscriber audiences.
self_serve_evidence: Any logged-in account holder can generate an API key immediately from account settings and start calling the API; OAuth2 is available for multi-account apps without a gated review step to obtain it.
api_surface: REST Marketing API covering campaigns, audiences/lists, automations, reports, templates, and e-commerce data — broad and mature.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community servers (112 tools in some); no official Mailchimp-maintained MCP found.
notes: API access can be limited by the authorizing user's account role, but this is account-level, not a platform approval gate.

one_liner: E-commerce-focused email and SMS marketing automation platform with customer data and event tracking.
self_serve_evidence: Private and public API keys are generated instantly and self-serve from account Settings with custom scopes; OAuth is only gated at the point of formal App Marketplace listing, not for basic API use.
api_surface: REST (JSON:API spec) covering 20+ resource categories — profiles, events, campaigns, flows, catalogs, metrics, coupons, forms, webhooks — with filtering, sparse fieldsets, and versioned releases; broad and modern.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Klaviyo-maintained MCP server, documented at developers.klaviyo.com/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server, offering hosted/local deployment and read-only/restricted modes.
notes: Having an official first-party MCP server makes this one of the most agent-ready apps in the set.

one_liner: All-in-one funnel builder and marketing platform (funnels, email, courses, affiliate management) for online businesses.
self_serve_evidence: Users generate a Public API key directly from dashboard profile settings and immediately authenticate via the X-API-Key header — no application or review process.
api_surface: REST API (cursor-paginated, JSON merge-patch support) covering contacts, tags, and related resources; narrower/still-evolving surface compared to larger platforms, with OAuth planned but not yet available.
existing_mcp_detail: Official systeme.io-hosted MCP server covering contacts, newsletters, funnels, price plans/coupons, and automation rules via MCP keys.
notes: API surface is comparatively narrow (contacts/tags-focused per current public docs) even though access itself is frictionless; official MCP already exists, which is notable for a smaller SaaS.

one_liner: Visual discovery/social platform API for managing pins, boards, ads, and analytics.
self_serve_evidence: Trial access (sandbox-only, self-serve after app registration with privacy policy) is the default, but Standard/production access requires submitting a video demonstration of the OAuth flow for manual review.
api_surface: REST API (v5) covering pins, boards, ads, audiences, catalogs, and user account management; moderately broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community servers exist; no official Pinterest MCP found.
blocker: Standard (production, non-sandbox) access requires a manual video-review approval process; Trial access limits all created content to sandbox-only visibility.
notes: Even single-user/internal integrations must complete the video-review step to escape the sandbox restriction, per Pinterest's own docs.

one_liner: Meta's Threads API for publishing posts, replies, and reading insights on the Threads text-based social app.
self_serve_evidence: threads_basic requires no review, but content publishing, reply management/reading, and insights permissions all require Meta App Review before any non-tester account can use them.
api_surface: REST-style Graph API surface covering post publishing, replies, insights/analytics; narrower than the full Facebook/Instagram Graph API but growing.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community servers exist; no official Meta-maintained Threads MCP found.
blocker: App Review is required for the permissions needed to actually publish/read content and insights for non-tester (real) users.
notes: Testers added under App Roles can use full functionality immediately without review, so prototyping/dev is unblocked even though public production use is gated.

one_liner: Twilio-owned transactional and marketing email delivery platform with an API for sending and managing email.
self_serve_evidence: Users create API keys instantly via account Settings and immediately authenticate with a Bearer token (or Basic Auth using 'apikey' as username) — no application/review step.
api_surface: REST v3 API covering transactional email sending, marketing campaigns, contacts/lists, templates, stats/analytics, and webhooks — broad and mature.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community servers exist; no official Twilio/SendGrid-maintained MCP found as of this research.
notes: One of the most frictionless integrations in this set — instant API key, well-documented REST surface, no approval gate.

one_liner: SaaS platform for building, hosting, and running online stores and their backend commerce operations.
self_serve_evidence: Merchants can self-serve generate custom-app access tokens directly in the Shopify Admin with no review, but public apps distributed via the Shopify App Store go through Shopify's partner review process.
api_surface: GraphQL Admin API (primary, very broad: products, orders, customers, inventory, fulfillment, checkout) plus a legacy REST Admin API and a separate Storefront API; extremely mature and well-documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Shopify/dev-mcp (official shopify.dev MCP server) and an official Storefront MCP for agentic shopping.
notes: One of the most agent-ready ecommerce APIs; Shopify is actively investing in first-party MCP tooling.

one_liner: Open-source e-commerce plugin that turns a WordPress site into an online store.
self_serve_evidence: Store owners generate REST API consumer key/secret pairs themselves under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API with no approval process.
api_surface: REST API (v1-v3) covering products, orders, customers, coupons, reports, and webhooks; since it's self-hosted, exact surface/version depends on each store's install and plugin version.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community servers exist.
notes: No central multi-tenant auth (each self-hosted store issues its own keys), but per-store integration is trivial and self-serve.

one_liner: SaaS e-commerce platform for building hosted or headless online stores.
self_serve_evidence: Merchants generate store-level API accounts directly in the control panel, and developers register apps via the Developer Portal without a hard approval gate to start building.
api_surface: REST (V2/V3 Admin) plus GraphQL (Storefront, Admin, and Account APIs); very broad coverage including products, orders, customers, carts, checkout, webhooks, and B2B.
existing_mcp_detail: BigCommerce's official Storefront MCP (launched 2026, natural-language product search/cart/checkout) plus community servers.
notes: BigCommerce is actively pushing agentic-commerce features; authenticated (logged-in) shopping via MCP is noted as coming next.

one_liner: Enterprise cloud commerce platform (B2C/B2B) used by large retail brands for storefronts and order management.
self_serve_evidence: SCAPI/OCAPI access requires an existing, Salesforce-provisioned B2C Commerce org/license plus SLAS or Account Manager credentials — there is no public self-serve signup for the commerce APIs themselves.
api_surface: SCAPI (REST, split into Shopper APIs and Admin APIs) plus legacy OCAPI; broad enterprise commerce coverage (catalog, cart, checkout, orders, customers, pricing, inventory) but scoped to a provisioned instance.
existing_mcp_detail: Community servers exist; no official Commerce-Cloud-specific MCP found (Salesforce's official MCP efforts so far target Agentforce/CRM and Marketing Cloud Engagement).
blocker: Requires an active, provisioned Salesforce B2C Commerce org/license and SLAS/Account Manager setup — no free shared sandbox for a generic third-party integrator.
notes: Enterprise-only platform; existing MCPs are community-built and some focus on developer assistance rather than full transactional coverage.

one_liner: Enterprise e-commerce platform available as self-hosted open source (Magento) or Adobe-managed SaaS (Adobe Commerce Cloud).
self_serve_evidence: Self-hosted Magento Open Source admins can generate integration tokens/OAuth 1.0a keys themselves with no external gate, but Adobe Commerce Cloud (SaaS) requires an Adobe-provisioned subscription/instance.
api_surface: REST API (broad: products, orders, customers, carts, inventory, CMS) plus a GraphQL API for storefront queries.
existing_mcp_detail: Numerous community servers reflecting strong developer demand.
blocker: Requires an existing Magento/Adobe Commerce instance to target — self-hosted setup overhead, or an Adobe Commerce Cloud subscription; no shared multi-tenant developer sandbox.
notes: Unusually large community MCP ecosystem (over a dozen servers found), reflecting strong developer demand despite the setup friction.

one_liner: Website builder and hosting platform with an integrated Commerce offering for online stores.
self_serve_evidence: Merchants on the Commerce Advanced plan can self-serve generate API keys in site settings, but full OAuth2 apps for third-party/commercial distribution require registering through Squarespace's developer program (a gated approval step).
api_surface: REST Commerce APIs covering Products, Orders, Inventory, Transactions, Profiles, Discounts, and Webhooks; only available on the Commerce Advanced plan.
existing_mcp_detail: Community servers exist (e.g. 67-tool Squarespace MCP Server).
blocker: API access is limited to merchants on the Commerce Advanced plan, and full OAuth app distribution requires Squarespace developer registration/approval.
notes: Plan-tier gating (Commerce Advanced only) is the main practical limiter rather than the auth mechanism itself.

one_liner: E-commerce platform (by Lightspeed) that lets merchants embed an online store into any website or social channel.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can register apps and obtain OAuth tokens via Ecwid's documented self-serve flow without a manual approval gate to start building/testing.
api_surface: REST API (JSON) covering store settings, products, categories, orders, customers, discounts, and payment/shipping methods; rate-limited to 600 requests/minute per token.
existing_mcp_detail: An Ecwid connector is listed on the Glama MCP directory.
notes: Smaller MCP community presence than the major platforms, but the core REST API itself is broad and self-serve.

one_liner: Simple e-commerce platform for independent creators to sell digital products, memberships, and subscriptions.
self_serve_evidence: Any Gumroad account holder can create an 'application' from account settings to generate an access token or set up OAuth2, with no approval process required.
api_surface: REST API covering products, sales, subscribers, offer codes, licenses, and resource subscriptions/webhooks — moderate breadth, single-seller focus.
existing_mcp_detail: keithah/gumroad-mcp — MCP server for the Gumroad API covering subscriptions, sales, and products.
notes: The primary help-center article is JS-rendered so full text couldn't be extracted directly; self-serve OAuth/token creation was corroborated via a working community MCP implementation.

one_liner: API suite for Amazon sellers and vendors to manage listings, orders, inventory, pricing, and reports on Amazon's marketplace.
self_serve_evidence: Registration requires submitting a developer profile, a security/data-protection questionnaire, and identity verification, with Amazon reviewing applications against policy and security requirements before granting access.
api_surface: REST APIs, very broad — orders, listings, catalog, inventory, pricing, reports, finances, fulfillment, and notifications — organized as many separate microservice-style API sections.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community servers exist.
blocker: Amazon's developer registration/approval process (identity verification, security review, role-based access) gates real API usage, especially for public/third-party apps.
notes: Private apps self-authorized by a seller for their own account are somewhat lighter-weight than public apps, but still require Solution Provider Portal registration and policy compliance.

one_liner: Creator/seller commerce and payments platform (checkout, funnels, subscriptions, affiliates, webinars) that rebranded from FanBasis to Commas in mid-2026.
self_serve_evidence: Commas opened free self-serve account signup at commas.com in 2026 (previously invite-only for sellers), but the developer API docs found sit behind a login wall and a fuller reference could not be fully accessed, so it's unconfirmed whether every account gets an API key or if API access is separately gated/manual.
api_surface: Evidence points to a REST-style API with a /products endpoint, checkout sessions, customers, subscriptions, discount codes, and webhooks, but no complete public reference could be verified end-to-end.
existing_mcp_detail: No dedicated MCP server for FanBasis/Commas was found.
blocker: Full endpoint/auth detail unconfirmed because apidocs.fan is a JS-rendered SPA, but a real, named 'Commas API Reference' (checkout sessions, webhooks, customers, subscriptions, discount codes) is publicly discoverable -- this is friction, not a hard block.
notes: This is the deliberately obscure app in the batch. Real API usage was confirmed indirectly via a third-party integration guide, but primary docs could not be reliably fetched/verified, so this is reported honestly as low-confidence rather than guessed. [Verified] apidocs.fan is a real, publicly reachable 'Commas API Reference' page, not merely an inaccessible wall as pass-1 implied -- pass-1 was too conservative here.

one_liner: DataForSEO is a data provider offering REST APIs for SERP data, keyword research, backlinks, on-page/domain analytics, and business/local data.
self_serve_evidence: Users create a free account and immediately get login/password API credentials from the dashboard, no sales contact required.
api_surface: Broad REST API family covering SERP, Keywords Data, Domain Analytics, Backlinks, On-Page, Business Data, App Data, and Content/AI Optimization endpoints, with client libraries in multiple languages.
existing_mcp_detail: Official DataForSEO MCP server (dataforseo.com/model-context-protocol), also listed on PulseMCP; several community MCP wrappers exist too.
notes: Simple, well-documented Basic Auth (base64 login:password) makes this one of the easier integrations; pricing is pay-as-you-go per API call.

one_liner: SE Ranking is an SEO platform (rank tracking, keyword/backlink/domain research, site audits) exposed via a Data API and a Project API.
self_serve_evidence: Any active subscription plan can generate an API key instantly from the API Dashboard, with no sales gate for standard access (enterprise volume needs sales).
api_surface: REST API with two surfaces (Data API and Project API) sharing one token; broad coverage of keyword research, backlinks, domain analysis, and rank tracking/project management.
existing_mcp_detail: Official centrally-hosted MCP server at api.seranking.com/mcp exposing 160+ tools, using OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration; also ships 7 Claude Skills.
notes: Core REST API uses simple Token-header API-key auth; the newer official MCP server layers OAuth 2.1 on top for agent access specifically.

one_liner: Ahrefs is an SEO toolset (Site Explorer, keyword research, rank tracking, backlink analysis) that exposes a REST API v3.
self_serve_evidence: API v3 access does not require an Enterprise plan or sales contact — it's available self-serve to Lite-tier and higher subscribers, with free test queries available before subscribing.
api_surface: REST API with a published OpenAPI spec; covers Site Explorer, keyword data, backlinks, rank tracking, and brand/AI-visibility monitoring; usage metered in API 'units' per plan.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Ahrefs MCP server (github.com/ahrefs/ahrefs-mcp-server; docs.ahrefs.com/en/mcp), also listed on PulseMCP.
notes: Requires an underlying paid Lite+ subscription (not free-tier), but that's a normal commercial gate, not a sales/approval gate.

one_liner: MrScraper is a smaller web-scraping SaaS offering a Google SERP scraper plus scrapers for e-commerce/travel marketplaces (Shopee, TikTok, Lazada, Booking.com, etc.).
self_serve_evidence: Docs reference a self-service dashboard (app.mrscraper.com) where users manage API tokens and usage; no sales-contact language found.
api_surface: REST API with sync and async Google SERP scraping endpoints, an async-result-retrieval endpoint, and additional vertical scrapers (marketplaces, travel, jobs); relatively narrow/niche compared to Apify/Bright Data.
existing_mcp_detail: No official or community MCP server found for MrScraper specifically.
blocker: It's a small, sparsely-documented vendor (docs.mrscraper.com has limited public detail on rate limits, pricing tiers, and full endpoint catalog) — genuinely obscure as flagged, so confidence in completeness is lower than the larger players.
notes: Real product with real docs (confirmed via docs.mrscraper.com), not fabricated, but it is a much smaller/lesser-known player than the other scraping vendors in this set, and no MCP ecosystem exists around it yet.

one_liner: Apify is a web-scraping and automation platform ('Actors') with a large marketplace of ready-made scrapers/crawlers accessible via REST API.
self_serve_evidence: Free account signup with self-serve API token generation in Apify Console; usage-based/free-tier pricing, no sales gate.
api_surface: Broad REST API covering Actor discovery/execution, dataset/key-value-store/log storage access, and thousands of community/first-party Actors (scrapers) as callable tools.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Apify MCP server hosted at mcp.apify.com, open-source at github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server, supports OAuth or bearer-token auth.
notes: One of the most agent-ready platforms researched; official MCP explicitly excludes full-permission and rental Actors for security/billing reasons.

one_liner: Firecrawl converts websites into clean, LLM-ready data via scrape/crawl/extract/search REST endpoints.
self_serve_evidence: Users generate an API key instantly at firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys; docs even describe an instant 'keyless' quick-start path with no signup required for trial use.
api_surface: REST API covering scrape, crawl, map, extract, and search operations; moderately broad and purpose-built for feeding LLMs/agents.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Firecrawl MCP server (github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server), documented at docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server.
notes: Explicitly designed for AI-agent consumption (LLM-ready markdown/JSON output), making it one of the most natural agent-toolkit fits in the set.

one_liner: Bright Data is a large web-data infrastructure platform offering proxies, a Web Unlocker, SERP API, Scraping Browser, and pre-built Scrapers.
self_serve_evidence: Signup and initial API access are immediate/self-serve with a free trial and recurring free tier, but full access to Proxy Networks and Web Unlocker is restricted until a payment method is verified.
api_surface: Broad REST API surface spanning Web Unlocker, SERP API, Scraping Browser, pre-built Scrapers, Functions, and a scraper Marketplace, with permission-scoped API keys (Admin/Finance/Ops/Limit/User).
existing_mcp_detail: Official Bright Data MCP server at github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp (also an official CLI at github.com/brightdata/cli); several community forks also exist.
blocker: Certain high-value products (Proxy Networks, Web Unlocker) require payment-method verification before full access, adding an onboarding step beyond pure self-serve.
notes: Large, mature API surface; the official MCP server and CLI both suggest strong agent-readiness despite the payment-verification friction.

one_liner: Sherlock is a free, open-source Python command-line tool that hunts for a given username across 400+ social networks.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can freely install it (pipx/Docker/package managers) and run it locally with no account, API key, or approval needed — but this is 'self-serve software install', not a hosted API signup.
api_surface: None. There is no hosted REST/GraphQL API — it's a local CLI/Python tool that queries each social platform directly and writes results to local files. A 2020-era GitHub issue proposed wrapping it as a REST API but this was never merged into the core project.
existing_mcp_detail: Claimed unofficial community MCP wrapper could not be independently corroborated via GitHub topics or MCP registries this pass -- downgraded from 'yes-community' pending stronger evidence.
blocker: No official hosted API exists to call — building an agent-toolkit integration means self-hosting/wrapping the CLI tool (subprocess execution, containerization, rate-limiting against target social sites yourself) rather than calling a vendor endpoint.
notes: Confirmed via the project's own README: it is explicitly a local CLI tool, not a SaaS/hosted API. Also carries legal/ethical/ToS risk since it queries third-party sites directly.

one_liner: Waterfall.io is a B2B contact/company data platform for finding and enriching contacts, prospecting by title/company, and verifying emails (a 'waterfall' enrichment provider, à la a Clay alternative).
self_serve_evidence: Docs describe a straightforward x-api-key header auth scheme against api.waterfall.io with full public endpoint documentation, implying self-service key issuance rather than sales gating, though the docs don't state this explicitly.
api_surface: REST API with roughly 13 documented endpoints split into synchronous (contact/company search, email verification, job-change detection, company reveal, admin/reporting) and asynchronous (prospecting, contact/phone/company enrichment) categories.
existing_mcp_detail: No official or community MCP server found for Waterfall.io itself.
notes: This is a genuinely small/niche vendor as flagged — docs.waterfall.io does exist and is real (confirmed live), but pricing/self-serve signup flow could not be independently confirmed beyond the API auth documentation itself, so confidence is medium rather than high.

one_liner: Clay is a go-to-market data/enrichment platform ('spreadsheet-like' tables) that combines 100+ data providers and AI agents for prospecting, enrichment, and outreach workflows, and now also exposes its own public API.
self_serve_evidence: Clay's own public API (Searches/Routines), launched July 2026, is self-serve via an API key on every plan including legacy ones, but the 'Tables' read primitive is Enterprise-plan only.
api_surface: REST-style public API (clay-api-key header) with inbound primitives — Searches (query Clay's database), Routines (run packaged workflow logic, async with polling/webhooks), and Tables (Enterprise-only read access) — plus a separate outbound HTTP API integration feature inside tables for calling arbitrary third-party APIs.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Clay MCP server built by Clay Labs Inc., exposing 200+ data providers/agents/workflows into ChatGPT, Claude, and Codex.
notes: Clay historically had no true outbound public API; this changed with a July 2026 public API/CLI/agent-plugin launch, which the official MCP server and this dataset should reflect as a recent but now-solid agent-integration surface. [Verified] Public API/CLI is real (~July 2026) but is an 'open beta' Agent Plugin, not confirmed GA on every plan; official terms are Clay API/CLI/Claygents, not 'Searches/Routines'. MCP provider count corrected to 200+.

one_liner: Git hosting and collaboration platform for source code, issues, pull requests, and CI/CD via Actions.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can create a personal access token or register an OAuth/GitHub App directly from developer settings with no vendor approval step.
api_surface: REST API (v3) with thousands of endpoints spanning repos, issues, PRs, Actions, orgs, etc., plus a GraphQL API (v4); one of the broadest developer APIs available.
existing_mcp_detail: github/github-mcp-server — GitHub's official MCP server (also listed in the github.com/mcp registry).
notes: Username/password auth is explicitly disallowed; fine-grained PATs and GitHub Apps are the recommended modern auth paths.

one_liner: Frontend cloud platform for building, deploying, and scaling web applications (especially Next.js).
self_serve_evidence: Any authenticated user can self-generate a bearer auth token via POST /v3/user/tokens from account settings, no approval required.
api_surface: REST API covering deployments, projects, domains, teams, env vars, access groups, and integrations, documented via an OpenAPI spec at openapi.vercel.sh; broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Vercel MCP, official remote MCP server at https://mcp.vercel.com with OAuth-based client authorization.
notes: MCP supports both public (unauthenticated) doc-search tools and authenticated project/deployment management tools.

one_liner: Platform for building, deploying, and hosting web apps and static sites with integrated CI/CD.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can generate a Personal Access Token from Applications settings with no approval workflow.
api_surface: REST API (OpenAPI-documented at open-api.netlify.com) covering sites, deploys, forms, DNS/SSL, env vars, and teams; comprehensive.
existing_mcp_detail: netlify/netlify-mcp (@netlify/mcp package) — Netlify's official MCP server for deploying and managing sites via AI agents.
notes: OAuth2 is required specifically for building public third-party integrations others can install; PATs suffice for direct/agent use.

one_liner: Global edge network providing CDN, DNS, security (WAF/Zero Trust), and serverless compute (Workers).
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can create scoped API Tokens (or legacy Global API Keys) directly from the dashboard without approval.
api_surface: Exclusively REST, roughly 2,500 endpoints across DNS, Workers, R2, KV, D1, Zero Trust/Access, WAF, Load Balancing, Stream, Images, AI Gateway, and more — very broad.
existing_mcp_detail: cloudflare/mcp — official token-efficient MCP server for the entire Cloudflare API, hosted at mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp using a search+execute code-mode pattern.
notes: Given the API's size, Cloudflare's own MCP avoids exposing thousands of individual tool schemas by using a query/execute pattern instead.

one_liner: Open-source backend-as-a-service providing a managed Postgres database, auth, storage, and edge functions.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can manually generate a Personal Access Token from their account page for immediate Management API use.
api_surface: Management/Admin REST API covering orgs, projects, database config, auth, storage, edge functions, and analytics, plus a separate auto-generated per-project PostgREST data API; broad.
existing_mcp_detail: Supabase MCP Server (supabase.com/docs/guides/ai-tools/mcp), officially maintained; also documented MCP OAuth authentication flow for connecting agents.
notes: Two distinct APIs exist: the Management API (project/org admin) and each project's own PostgREST data API (uses anon/service_role API keys).

one_liner: Native graph database platform for storing and querying highly connected data via the Cypher query language.
self_serve_evidence: Aura free-tier instances and Aura API OAuth credentials are self-serve, but Enterprise/on-prem Cypher access typically relies on admin-provisioned username/password credentials.
api_surface: No single broad public REST management API like the other apps; primary data access is Cypher over the Bolt protocol via drivers, with an HTTP Query API and a separate Aura Admin (REST) API for cloud instance lifecycle management — narrower and more fragmented than typical SaaS admin APIs.
existing_mcp_detail: neo4j/mcp — Neo4j's official MCP server (Go-based), documented at neo4j.com/docs/mcp with HTTP Bearer/Basic auth support.
blocker: No single broad self-serve REST/HTTP data API — core interaction is via Bolt-protocol drivers rather than simple HTTP calls, and Aura cloud-management is a separate API from data-plane Cypher access.
notes: Confirmed MCP auth (Basic for Community, Bearer/SSO for Aura/Enterprise) directly from docs; did not independently fetch Aura Admin API auth specifics, so self-serve nuance for cloud provisioning is medium confidence.

one_liner: Cloud data platform (data warehouse) for storing, querying, and sharing structured and semi-structured data at scale.
self_serve_evidence: A Snowflake account (including a self-serve free trial) is easy to get, but key-pair/OAuth/workload-identity auth setup for API access typically requires ACCOUNTADMIN-level configuration.
api_surface: Multiple REST API families — the SQL API (execute statements), object-management REST APIs (databases, warehouses, users), and Cortex APIs — broad in total but fragmented rather than one unified surface.
existing_mcp_detail: Snowflake's official Cortex Agents MCP Server; the earlier community Snowflake-Labs/mcp repo is now deprecated in favor of it.
blocker: Auth setup (key-pair generation, OAuth integration, or workload identity federation) generally requires admin-role configuration, and using the API requires a running (billed) virtual warehouse.
notes: Programmatic Access Tokens (PATs) are the simplest self-serve bearer-token option; JWT/key-pair and WIF are more enterprise-oriented.

one_liner: Fully managed cloud database service for MongoDB, handling cluster provisioning, scaling, and operations.
self_serve_evidence: Any Atlas org owner can self-generate API keys or OAuth2 service-account credentials directly from project/org settings, no vendor approval needed.
api_surface: Atlas Administration API (REST, OpenAPI-documented) covering clusters, backups, database users, alerts, billing, and org/project management; broad but infra-only — it explicitly does not expose the data plane.
existing_mcp_detail: MongoDB MCP Server (official, docs.mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server), supports both Atlas administration and data queries/exploration.
blocker: The Admin API manages infrastructure only, not database contents — reading/writing actual data requires a separate MongoDB wire-protocol driver connection with its own auth, not simple REST calls.
notes: OAuth2 Service Accounts (client-credentials flow) are now recommended over legacy API keys, which use HTTP Digest authentication.

one_liner: Cloud monitoring and observability platform for infrastructure, application performance, and log data.
self_serve_evidence: Any account holder can generate API and Application keys directly from account settings, with no approval workflow described in the docs.
api_surface: REST API (v1/v2) covering monitors, dashboards, metrics, logs, incidents, security signals, and APM configuration; very broad, hundreds of endpoints.
existing_mcp_detail: Datadog MCP Server (official, docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/), bridging observability data to MCP-compatible AI agents; a separate Code Security MCP server also exists.
notes: Requires two distinct credentials — an API key (write/report) and an Application key (read/full access) — passed together, rather than a single token.

one_liner: Application error tracking and performance monitoring platform for developers.
self_serve_evidence: Users can self-generate auth tokens (personal or internal-integration tokens) or register OAuth2 apps directly from account/org settings with no approval step.
api_surface: REST API covering issues, events, projects, organizations, releases, and alerts; broad and well documented.
existing_mcp_detail: getsentry/sentry-mcp — Sentry's official MCP server, positioned as middleware over the Sentry API for coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor.
notes: Also supports RFC 8628 device authorization flow for CLI/headless clients; legacy Basic-Auth API keys are deprecated for new accounts in favor of tokens/OAuth2.

one_liner: All-in-one workspace app combining notes, docs, wikis, and lightweight databases/project trackers.
self_serve_evidence: Any user can create an internal integration or personal access token instantly, and public OAuth integrations are self-serve to build (bearer-token auth) though listing in the public integrations gallery involves Notion review.
api_surface: REST/HTTP API (developers.notion.com) covering pages, databases/data sources, blocks, users, comments and search; moderately broad and well-documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Notion MCP — remote hosted server at mcp.notion.com (OAuth) plus open-source 'Official Notion MCP Server' repo under github.com/makenotion/notion-mcp-server.
notes: Three auth flavors: internal integration bot tokens, personal access tokens (act as the user), and OAuth for public/third-party apps.

one_liner: Spreadsheet-database hybrid ('no-code app platform') for organizing structured data and workflows.
self_serve_evidence: Personal access tokens are created instantly via the developer hub (airtable.com/create/tokens) with scoped, granular permissions; OAuth apps for third parties are also self-serve to register.
api_surface: REST Web API (airtable.com/developers/web/api) covering bases, tables, records, fields, schema, and webhooks; broad and actively maintained.
existing_mcp_detail: Official '@airtable/mcp-cli' (npm, maintained by airtable.com staff) auto-discovers tools from Airtable's own hosted MCP server; explicitly marked experimental/subject to change.
notes: Enterprise-only 'enterprise.*' scopes exist on top of the standard scope set; MCP server/CLI is labeled experimental.

one_liner: Issue tracking and project management tool purpose-built for software engineering teams.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can self-serve create OAuth2 applications from workspace settings and generate personal API keys with no approval process.
api_surface: GraphQL API (developers.linear.app) covering issues, projects, teams, cycles, comments, and webhooks; broad single-endpoint GraphQL schema.
existing_mcp_detail: Official remote MCP server at mcp.linear.app/mcp (read-write) and mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly, using Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.1 or API key auth.
notes: GraphQL-only API; OAuth tokens valid 24h with refresh tokens, plus PKCE and client-credentials support.

one_liner: Issue and project tracking tool for software development and agile teams, part of Atlassian Cloud.
self_serve_evidence: API tokens are self-generated at id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens for basic auth, and OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps are created self-serve via the Atlassian developer console.
api_surface: REST API v3 (developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira) — very broad, covering issues, projects, workflows, users, JQL search, webhooks, and app frameworks (Forge/Connect).
existing_mcp_detail: Atlassian Remote MCP Server (Rovo) — official OAuth-secured proxy connecting AI clients to Jira and Confluence, available to all Atlassian Cloud customers with plan-based rate limits.
notes: Atlassian discourages token-based basic auth for production apps and recommends OAuth 2.0/Forge/Connect for anything distributed to other customers.

one_liner: Work management platform for tracking team tasks, projects, and portfolios.
self_serve_evidence: Personal access tokens are generated directly from the developer console with no approval step; OAuth/OIDC apps are also self-registered, while only Service Accounts require Enterprise admin provisioning.
api_surface: REST API (developers.asana.com) covering tasks, projects, portfolios, workspaces, custom fields and webhooks; broad and mature.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Asana MCP server documented at developers.asana.com/docs/using-the-asana-mcp-server, exposing the Asana Work Graph to MCP-compatible AI clients.
notes: Service Accounts (full-account access) are Enterprise-tier and admin-provisioned only; standard PAT/OAuth paths are open to all plans.

one_liner: Cloud-based 'work OS' / no-code platform for managing boards, tasks, and team workflows.
self_serve_evidence: Any user can generate a personal V2 API token from their profile's Developer settings without approval, and OAuth apps are self-registered in the developer center.
api_surface: GraphQL API v2 (developer.monday.com) covering boards, items, columns, users, docs, and webhooks; broad and actively documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Official 'Platform MCP' hosted remote server at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp (OAuth 2.1 or bearer token) plus a local 'Apps MCP' for app development.
notes: Token permissions mirror whatever the underlying user can do in the monday.com UI.

one_liner: All-in-one productivity and project management platform combining tasks, docs, goals, and time tracking.
self_serve_evidence: Personal API tokens (pk_ prefix) are generated instantly from account Settings > Apps; OAuth2 app registration requires only Workspace owner/admin rights, no ClickUp approval.
api_surface: REST API v2 (developer.clickup.com) covering tasks, spaces, docs, goals, time tracking, and webhooks; broad and widely used.
existing_mcp_detail: ClickUp now ships an official first-party MCP server at mcp.clickup.com/mcp (OAuth 2.1+PKCE, public beta, available on all plans), documented at developer.clickup.com. The community package @taazkareem/clickup-mcp-server (~100k+ monthly downloads) remains a popular independent alternative.
notes: OAuth access tokens currently don't expire ('subject to change' per docs); verified via npm registry that no official @clickup-scoped MCP package exists.

one_liner: All-in-one doc that blends documents, spreadsheets, and lightweight app-building (Packs).
self_serve_evidence: Any Coda user can generate a bearer API token from account settings with no approval process, though token capabilities are limited by the user's workspace role (e.g., Doc Maker/Admin for doc creation).
api_surface: REST API (coda.io/developers/apis/v1) covering docs, tables, rows, formulas, and automations; moderate breadth compared to larger PM tools, plus a separate Packs SDK for building connectors with OAuth support.
existing_mcp_detail: No official Coda MCP found; leading community option is 'coda-mcp' (npm, maintainer orellazri), alongside several smaller community forks.
notes: Coda's own developer portal blocks automated fetching (robots.txt); details confirmed via the API v1 reference page and npm registry checks instead.

one_liner: Spreadsheet-style work management and automation platform for sheets, reports, and dashboards.
self_serve_evidence: Basic API access tokens are self-serve to generate in the UI, but the official MCP server and some premium capabilities require a Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management plan.
api_surface: REST API v2 (developers.smartsheet.com) covering sheets, rows, reports, dashboards, webhooks, and admin/user management; broad and well-documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Smartsheet MCP server; a prior community project 'smar-mcp' was deprecated in favor of it.
blocker: Official MCP server (and some premium API-adjacent features) require a paid Business/Enterprise/Advanced Work Management plan.
notes: Core REST API auth itself (access tokens, OAuth) is self-serve regardless of plan; the gating is specifically on the MCP offering per Smartsheet's docs.

one_liner: Time tracking and invoicing software for teams, freelancers, and agencies.
self_serve_evidence: Personal Access Tokens and OAuth2 applications are both created directly from the Developers section of Harvest ID with no manual approval required.
api_surface: REST API v2 (help.getharvest.com/api-v2) covering time entries, projects, clients, invoices, expenses, and users; moderate breadth, focused on time/billing workflows.
existing_mcp_detail: No official Harvest MCP found; multiple community servers exist on npm.
notes: Server-side apps use Authorization Code flow; client-side apps use Implicit Grant; both PAT and OAuth requests require an Account-ID header alongside the token.

one_liner: Stripe is a payments and financial infrastructure platform providing APIs for online payments, billing, invoicing, and money movement.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can create a Stripe account and immediately obtain test-mode and live-mode API keys from the Dashboard with no approval gate.
api_surface: Very broad REST API (v1 plus newer v2 'Money Management' resources) covering payments, customers, invoices/billing, subscriptions, Connect, tax, issuing, treasury, and more; keys authenticate via HTTP Basic Auth (key as username) or Bearer token.
existing_mcp_detail: Official remote MCP server at https://mcp.stripe.com (OAuth or restricted-key bearer auth), documented at docs.stripe.com/mcp, exposing tools like stripe_api_read/write, create_refund, stripe_report, etc.
notes: One of the most agent-ready APIs researched; official MCP already supports read/write across most core resources with restricted-key scoping for safety.

one_liner: Plaid provides APIs for connecting to users' bank accounts to retrieve balances, transactions, identity, income, and other financial data.
self_serve_evidence: Sandbox environment and client_id/secret are available immediately on signup, but Production API access must be explicitly requested and approved via the Dashboard.
api_surface: REST API (JSON over HTTPS, POST-based) spanning Auth, Transactions, Identity, Investments, Liabilities, Income, Transfer, Identity Verification, and more — broad product surface but narrow per-endpoint design.
existing_mcp_detail: Plaid's own GitHub org publishes an MCP server (plaid/ai-coding-toolkit, sandbox MCP server) plus several active community Plaid MCP servers (e.g. 304techmaven/plaid-mcp-server).
blocker: Production access requires Plaid's approval/review process even though sandbox is instant and free.
notes: MCP-server search tools returned inconsistent/possibly non-functional query results, so absence of a Plaid MCP should be treated as 'not found' rather than definitively 'does not exist'.

one_liner: Binance is a cryptocurrency exchange offering APIs for spot/futures/margin trading, market data, wallet, and payment services.
self_serve_evidence: Users generate API keys directly from account security settings immediately after standard account signup/KYC, with no separate developer-approval step for core spot trading and market data endpoints.
api_surface: Very broad REST + WebSocket APIs covering spot, margin, USDⓈ-M/COIN-M futures, wallet management, sub-accounts, and Binance Pay; requests are authenticated with an API key plus HMAC-SHA256/RSA/Ed25519 request signing (OAuth used separately for Binance Connect/Pay third-party apps).
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers exist; no official Binance-built MCP found.
notes: Signed-request (HMAC/RSA) auth is more complex than plain API keys but is a well-documented, standard pattern with abundant SDK support.

one_liner: Paygent Connect appears to be a payment-processing offering associated with the 'Paygent' merchant-services brand (paygent.co.uk) said to be built on NMI's white-label gateway infrastructure, but no distinct public developer documentation could be located.
self_serve_evidence: No public self-serve developer portal, signup page, or API reference for 'Paygent Connect' was found; the underlying NMI gateway it is reportedly powered by requires a partner/merchant application and automated risk review before issuing Gateway/Merchant IDs.
api_surface: Unconfirmed for Paygent Connect specifically. If it inherits NMI's gateway, the underlying surface would be NMI's REST APIs (v5 payments/invoicing/subscriptions/customers), a Query API for reporting, Direct Post, and webhooks — but this could not be verified as applying to 'Paygent Connect' itself.
existing_mcp_detail: No MCP server found for Paygent, Paygent Connect, or NMI.
blocker: No discoverable public developer documentation, self-serve signup, or confirmed API identity for 'Paygent Connect' as a distinct product (paygentconnect.com does not even resolve).
notes: Honest disclosure: could not confirm 'Paygent Connect' as a standalone product with public API docs. Closest matches were paygent.co.uk (a UK merchant-services/ISO brand) and NMI's own gateway, which is itself a gated partner/reseller program (automated risk review required). This matches the task's expectation that some obscure payment-orchestration brands lack a real public self-serve developer program. [Verified] docs.nmi.com was mischaracterized in pass-1 as a 'gated partner gateway' -- it is actually publicly accessible developer documentation with an open quickstart/sandbox; corrected here. The core finding (Paygent Connect itself is not independently findable) held up.

one_liner: iPayX is a FINTRAC-registered FX (foreign-exchange) fee-auditing/verification service that compares rates applied by banks or card networks against real-time mid-market rates for cross-border transactions.
self_serve_evidence: Core mid-market-rate/FX-audit functionality works with no authentication at all; an optional API key for 'live provider comparisons' is described as obtainable at ipayx.ai, but no public self-serve signup flow, pricing page content, or formal API reference could be confirmed.
api_surface: Narrow and not formally documented as a general REST API — primary public interface is an MCP server (four tools: audit FX fees, compare live quotes across providers like Wise/OFX/Airwallex, score invoice FX-fairness, retrieve ECB mid-market rates); no public REST API reference site was found.
existing_mcp_detail: @ipayx/mcp-fx-audit (GitHub: Ipayx-stellar/mcp-fx-audit), MIT-licensed, published under the company's own org and documented at ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server; installable via npm or Smithery.
blocker: Very early-stage/niche product (single-commit repo, 0 stars/forks at time of research) with no formal public API reference beyond the MCP tool descriptions and marketing site; not a full payment-orchestration API.
notes: iPayX is not a traditional payments/processing API in the Stripe/Plaid sense — it's a small FX-fee-audit/verification tool. Its MCP server is real and installable today, which is unusual for such an obscure product, but the underlying data/business is thin and unverified beyond the MCP repo and marketing pages.

one_liner: QuickBooks Online is Intuit's cloud accounting software, exposing a REST API for invoices, customers, vendors, payments, and other accounting data.
self_serve_evidence: A free Intuit Developer account grants an instant sandbox company plus OAuth2 client ID/secret; production keys are similarly self-serve for a private connection, but publicly listing an app on the QuickBooks App Store requires Intuit's app review/certification process.
api_surface: Broad REST API covering the accounting data model — invoices, customers, bills, vendors, accounts, payments, P&L/financial reports — with CRUD operations, a query language, webhooks, and batch processing.
existing_mcp_detail: No dedicated official (Intuit-built) or clearly-established community QuickBooks-specific MCP server was confirmed; only a general multi-app connector platform lists QuickBooks as one of many supported integrations.
blocker: none for a private/internal agent integration; app-store certification is only required for public distribution.
notes: The official developer.intuit.com pages are heavily JS-rendered and did not return readable text via fetch; auth/sandbox details were corroborated via a third-party integration guide describing the same OAuth2 flow and self-serve sandbox creation.

one_liner: Xero is cloud accounting software providing a REST API for accounting, payroll, assets, projects, and file data.
self_serve_evidence: Any developer can sign up for a free Xero account, spin up a demo/sandbox company, and self-register an OAuth2 app to get a client ID/secret with no approval step; Xero explicitly does not support basic API-key auth, only OAuth2.
api_surface: Broad REST API — Accounting API, Payroll API, Assets, Projects, Files, Bank Feeds — with official SDKs in multiple languages.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Xero MCP server (GitHub: XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server), supporting 50+ MCP commands across contacts, chart of accounts, invoices, and payroll, with Custom Connection or Bearer Token OAuth2 auth.
notes: Very agent-ready: self-serve OAuth2, sandbox demo company, and an official first-party MCP server maintained under the XeroAPI GitHub org.

one_liner: Brex is a corporate card and spend-management platform offering an API for expenses, payments, cards, and accounting data.
self_serve_evidence: The official quickstart states the guide 'assumes you are a Brex customer with admin access to your dashboard' — a user token can only be generated by an existing Brex account/card admin after the company accepts the developer API agreement; OAuth is offered separately for approved partner applications.
api_surface: Broad REST API spanning Accounting, Budgets & Limits, Expenses, Onboarding, Payments (ACH/wire/check), Team, Transactions, Travel, and Webhooks.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Brex MCP server (beta), documented at developer.brex.com/docs/mcp, supporting expense/card/transaction/bill/travel tools via OAuth (recommended) or API-key bearer token.
blocker: Requires an existing Brex corporate account with admin privileges (or approved partner OAuth relationship) to obtain credentials — not open to arbitrary third-party developers without a Brex business relationship.
notes: Despite the customer-gated access, Brex has invested in agent readiness with an official MCP server already in beta.

one_liner: Ramp is a corporate card and spend-management platform offering a developer API for cards, transactions, bills, and accounting data.
self_serve_evidence: Ramp's own docs state sandbox access 'is not self-serve — to get a sandbox environment, contact your account manager,' and third-party developer accounts cannot connect to production apps without going through an application/approval process.
api_surface: REST API (OAuth2 client-credentials grant with scoped access) covering cards, transactions, bills, reimbursements, users, and accounting integrations per docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1.
existing_mcp_detail: Official ramp_mcp repository under the ramp-public GitHub org (33 stars/19 forks), alongside a ramp-cli and mcp-skills repo also published by Ramp.
blocker: Sandbox and production API access require explicit account-manager/partner approval even though OAuth app registration in the dashboard itself is self-serve.
notes: Ramp has an official, actively maintained MCP server, but real usage is blocked behind account-manager-gated sandbox/production access.

one_liner: PitchBook is a private and public capital-markets data platform; its API provides programmatic access to deals, investors, funds, people, and company data.
